description: dtp/order@1 fixtures. A conforming validator MUST accept every body under "accept" and refuse every body under "reject"; it MUST accept a genesis only when "genesis.accept" says so; given a previous and a next revision of one order it MUST accept every pair under "continuity.accept" and refuse every pair under "continuity.reject". Refusal reasons are not normative. An order is a binding commercial commitment: a forecast or a plan is never an order.

accept.why: a purchase order the company placed with a supplier: two lines, one by product revision in cases, one by description
a sales order a customer placed with the company, recorded by the company as seller
the minimum: one line by description, no price, no window, no terms
an order that replaces an earlier one and cites a contract
an acknowledged order, as a later revision would carry it

reject.why: the company itself with a party record
a counterparty without a party record
a placing time that is not a UTC instant
a line with neither product nor description
a product revision without its root
a window that ends before it starts
a window with an impossible date
a payment term beyond a year
an incoterm that is not three letters
an order cannot be born acknowledged

accept.why: edited while placed: a line added and a term changed
partially fulfilled, then again, then fulfilled, then closed: the seller's own identifier learned on the way

reject.why: lines changed after acknowledgment: a change is a new order
